topics.narration: No waiter, no menu at the table. In Japan, you feed the machine first — then you sit down.
topics.rule: Buy your meal ticket first, then sit.
topics.title: POV: your first ramen in Japan

topics.narration: A dish arrives that nobody ordered — and everyone pays for it. It's not a scam. It's the cover charge.
topics.rule: Everyone pays for a dish nobody ordered: the otoshi is the table charge.
topics.title: POV: your first izakaya in Japan

topics.rule: A friendly guy says he knows a cheap bar. Don't follow him.
topics.narration: He's friendly, he speaks English, and the bar is just over here. Follow him, and the cheap drink costs five hundred dollars.
topics.title: POV: your first night out in Tokyo

topics.narration: Don't drown the nigiri. Turn it over, dip the fish — just a touch — and eat it in one bite.
topics.rule: Don't drown the nigiri in soy sauce; dip the fish side, lightly.
topics.title: POV: your first sushi in Japan

topics.narration: In Japan, you don't hand cash to the clerk. It goes on the little blue tray — and your change comes back on it.
topics.rule: Cash goes on the tray, not in the clerk's hand.
topics.title: POV: your first konbini in Japan

topics.narration: They ask one question before you pay: bag? Say yes and it costs 3 yen — and your warm and cold food never share a bag.
topics.rule: They ask "bag?" — a bag costs 3 yen; warm and cold items get separate bags.
topics.title: POV: your first konbini in Japan

topics.rule: Don't buy a ticket every ride. Get the card — or put it in your phone.
topics.narration: Every ride starts with a fare chart you can't read. One tap card ends all of it — trains, buses, even the konbini.
topics.title: POV: your first train ride in Japan

topics.rule: Skip the customs line — the QR code is filled in before you land.
topics.narration: Everyone lands and starts writing on paper. You did it on the plane: one QR code, and you walk past the whole line.
topics.title: POV: your first arrival in Japan

topics.narration: Don't insert the card. Tap it — and if the gate beeps red, you charge it here, not at the gate with a line behind you.
topics.rule: Tap, don't insert; charge before the gate, not at it.
topics.title: POV: your first train station in Japan

topics.scene: conveyor sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi), plates circling on the belt
topics.rule: A plate you take off the belt is yours — never put it back.
topics.narration: You grabbed a plate, changed your mind, and slid it back onto the belt. In Japan, the plate is yours the moment you touch it — cameras watch the belt, and a plate that looks tampered with gets pulled.
topics.title: POV: your first conveyor sushi in Japan

topics.rule: Don't tip. Ever. There is no tip jar — service is already in the price.
topics.narration: You leave cash on the table and walk out. Seconds later the waiter runs after you — you forgot your money. Tipping doesn't exist here.
topics.title: POV: your first restaurant bill in Japan

topics.narration: The water is free. The tea is free. And nobody is coming to take your order for them — help yourself.
topics.rule: Water and tea are free and often self-serve; nobody brings a bill for them.
topics.title: POV: your first restaurant in Japan

topics.narration: See those lines on the platform? Stand in them. And when the doors open — everyone gets off before anyone gets on.
topics.rule: Stand in the marked lines on the platform; let everyone off first.
topics.title: POV: your first train in Japan

topics.narration: You tap your IC card and the gate slams shut — the balance is empty, and the whole rush-hour line is behind you. Charge it before the gate, not at it.
topics.rule: Charge your IC card before the gate — an empty balance slams it shut with the line behind you.
topics.title: POV: your first ticket gate in Japan

topics.narration: At a Japanese buffet, the tray comes first — and every round gets a fresh plate. No exceptions.
topics.rule: At a buffet, take a tray first; new plate for each round.
topics.title: POV: your first buffet in Japan

topics.narration: Before the total, before the money, comes the question: point card? Miss it, and the points are gone forever.
topics.rule: "Point card?" (ポイントカードはお持ちですか？) comes before you pay.
topics.title: POV: your first konbini in Japan

topics.narration: Don't hand the cashier your basket. Put it on the stand, step back, and watch the system work.
topics.rule: In a supermarket, put your basket on the stand — don't hand it over.
topics.title: POV: your first supermarket in Japan

topics.narration: Need the staff? Don't wait quietly. Call out sumimasen — nice and loud. It's not rude. It's the system.
topics.rule: To call staff, say sumimasen loudly — it's not rude, it's the system.
topics.title: POV: your first restaurant in Japan

topics.narration: The wet towel is for your hands — only your hands. Not your face, not the table, not your phone.
topics.rule: The wet towel is for your hands, not your face.
topics.title: POV: your first restaurant in Japan

topics.narration: Ten thousand people eating street food — and almost no trash cans. Your garbage goes home in your bag.
topics.rule: At festivals there are almost no trash cans; carry your garbage home.
topics.title: POV: your first festival in Japan

topics.narration: Two bows, two claps, one wish, one bow. Get the order wrong and the whole shrine knows you're new here.
topics.rule: At the shrine: bow twice, clap twice, pray, bow once.
topics.title: POV: your first shrine visit in Japan

topics.scene: Japanese family restaurant table, rice bowl
topics.rule: Never stick your chopsticks upright in rice — it looks like a funeral offering.
topics.narration: You stick your chopsticks upright in the rice bowl. Everyone freezes — upright chopsticks are only for the dead.
topics.title: POV: your first meal in Japan

topics.rule: Slurp your noodles — loudly. Silence means you didn't like them.
topics.narration: You eat your ramen in silence, politely. The chef looks worried — in Japan, loud slurping means you love it.
topics.title: POV: your first ramen in Japan

topics.rule: Never pour your own beer — pour for others, and hold your glass with two hands.
topics.narration: You pour your own beer. Everyone stares — in Japan you pour for others, and they pour for you.
topics.title: POV: your first izakaya in Japan

topics.narration: A full train, and you can hear a pin drop. Your phone goes on manner mode — and your calls wait for the platform.
topics.rule: Phone on silent (manner mode); no calls on the train.
topics.title: POV: your first train in Japan

topics.rule: Stand on the left in Tokyo — the right in Osaka. One side stays open.
topics.narration: Stand on the wrong side and the whole city queues behind you in silence. Tokyo stands left, Osaka stands right — and one lane is always for walking.
topics.title: POV: your first escalator in Japan

topics.narration: On this bus, you don't pay to get on. You pay to get off — one flat fare, at the front, on your way out.
topics.rule: On many city buses you pay when you get OFF — flat fare at the front.
topics.title: POV: your first bus in Japan

topics.rule: Check your seat number — a reserved seat belongs to someone.
topics.narration: You sit down on the bullet train. Then the real passenger arrives — and the whole car knows you're in the wrong seat.
topics.title: POV: your first bullet train in Japan

topics.rule: Photos of the maids are off limits — the photo is on the menu, a cheki you pay for.
topics.narration: You raise your camera at your maid. Then the whole cafe knows — her photo is on the menu, and you pay for it.
topics.title: POV: your first maid cafe in Japan

topics.rule: Don't hold deer crackers up high to make the deer bow — hold them low, and watch out for headbutts.
topics.narration: You hold the crackers up high to make the deer bow. Then the whole herd crowds in — hold them low, and the deer bows for you.
topics.title: POV: your first deer crackers in Nara

topics.rule: Don't speak or stick your head through the window — circle your order, press the call button.
topics.narration: You stick your head through the kitchen window to order. Then the whole booth knows — at a solo ramen booth, you don't say a word.
topics.title: POV: your first solo ramen booth in Japan

topics.narration: At a sushi counter, the chef has already put wasabi under the fish — there's no need to stir more into your soy sauce.
topics.rule: Don't stir wasabi into your soy sauce — the chef already put it under the fish.
topics.title: POV: your first sushi counter in Japan

topics.rule: Udon shops are self-service — but not THAT self-service. Take a tray, order at the counter, add tempura with the tongs, pay at the end.
topics.narration: You served yourself straight from the kitchen. In Japan, udon is self-service — just not that self-service.
topics.title: POV: your first udon shop in Japan
